summary.headline: Orders and revenue beat target this week, but revenue remains behind target for the quarter and year, with new signups down 10.8% WoW.

points.what: Orders were 101.2% of target and revenue was 108.7% of target this week.
points.so_what: This puts the week ahead of target on both measures, unlike the quarter and year positions, which remain behind target.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue are both at 90.0% of target.
points.so_what: An ahead week has not closed the gap for the quarter or the year, both of which remain behind target.

points.what: New signups fell 10.8% WoW to 256, while orders rose 3.5% WoW.
points.so_what: Signups are the weak spot in an otherwise ahead-of-target week.

points.what: The recent 8-week revenue run-rate remains below the pace required to reach the full-year target.
points.so_what: This keeps the full-year target at risk even after an ahead-of-target week.

points.what: QTD revenue needs $296,595 more to reach the full-quarter target, with 4 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: This leaves a meaningful gap to close in the remaining weeks of the quarter.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate is $53,830, below the $77,519 weekly rate required for the rest of the year against target.
points.so_what: At the current pace, the full-year target is at risk.

points.what: New signups fell 10.8% WoW to 256, a notable decline.
points.so_what: This is a risk to new customer growth even as overall orders stayed ahead of target this week.

points.what: Orders were 101.2% of target and revenue was 108.7% of target this week.
points.so_what: The week was ahead of target on both measures, contrasting with the quarter and year positions below.

points.what: QTD revenue is 90.0% of target and YTD revenue is also 90.0% of target, both behind target.
points.so_what: Despite the ahead week, the quarter and year remain behind target, so one strong week has not been enough to close the gap.

points.what: The required weekly revenue run-rate to hit the full-year target is $77,519, while the current 8-week run-rate is $53,830.
points.so_what: The recent pace is well below what's needed, making the full-year target harder to reach at the current trend.

points.what: LATAM orders rose 25.2% WoW and was the top regional contributor to the week's order growth, accounting for 96.4% of the total change.
points.so_what: Order growth this week relied heavily on one region rather than being broad-based across APAC, North America, and EMEA.

points.what: Search orders rose 4.7% WoW and was the top traffic-source contributor, accounting for 92.9% of the change.
points.so_what: Growth continues to concentrate in the largest channel rather than being spread across other traffic sources.

points.what: Facebook orders fell 27.3% WoW, the largest negative contributor at -64.3% of the change.
points.so_what: This decline pulled against the gains from Search and LATAM, showing the order increase was not uniform across traffic sources.

points.what: AOV was $89.50, up 7.2% WoW, but down 1.2% YoY from $90.55 last year.
points.so_what: This week's revenue gain got a boost from a higher basket value, though AOV remains below where it was a year ago.

points.what: Cancellation rate fell 4.7pp WoW to 14.3%, and is down 2.4pp YoY from 16.7% last year.
points.so_what: Each point of cancellation is worth $731 in revenue, so the drop in cancellations supported this week's revenue result.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 2026-02-09 was 10.8%, flat WoW but up 1.5pp YoY from 9.3%.
points.so_what: Returns are running higher than the same week last year, a bad-direction signal on order quality.

points.what: New signups rose 9.9% YoY while orders rose 62.1% YoY.
points.so_what: New customer growth continues to lag far behind order growth this year.
